newsitem.title: GERMANY: Central America feels pinch from low coffee prices.
newsitem.headline: Central America feels pinch from low coffee prices.

text.p: Central American coffee industries lacked necessary capital because global coffee prices were low and because they were spending money on producer retention schemes, a Honduran official said.
"We bear the retention costs to help stabilise the market, which saves someone at the other end a few dollars," said Maritza Midence of the Honduras Coffee Institute (IHCAFE).
"These monies should be spent on fighting the rise of other beverages," she told the F.O. Licht Coffee Conference, which highlighted flat global consumption trends.
Midence said coffee prices had deteriorated in 1995/96 despite retention, a harsh winter in consuming countries, smaller crops in Brazil and Colombia, and low consumer stocks.
Harvests in Central America had been stable compared with the previous year but lower output was expected for 96/97.
She cited Hurricane Caesar, which hit Costa Rican production, and a slow-down in the natural production cycle.

The region remained committed to expanding production, especially of premium grades, although interest rates were crippling, labour was attracted away from the coffee sector and only Nicaragua and Honduras had additional land reserves.
The region, which supplies 12 percent of the world's so-called mild coffees, was forecast to produce 10.9 million bags of green coffee in 1996/97 after 11.1 million in 95/96, IHCAFE figures showed.
